answer: Per-identity challenge escrow makes every new agent prepay a fixed compute rent released only after completing a rotating zephyr challenge workload. Clones must forge separate identities and pay that rent each time, so the attacker cannot amortize one prepayment across many agents. Enforcement consumes the prepaid rent on any challenge failure, and the required rent is calibrated above expected session profit until the marginal clone’s expected value reaches its nadir and is strictly negative.
